topics.title: Oil spike rattles markets
topics.summary: Oil moved above $100 a barrel as Middle East tensions raised supply worries, pressuring stocks and putting fresh attention on inflation and household fuel costs.
topics.discussionPrompt: If gas prices suddenly become the studio's main villain, who starts budgeting and who just blames the coffee run?

topics.title: Wall Street loses ground
topics.summary: Major U.S. stock indexes slipped as higher crude prices and rising Treasury yields made investors cautious ahead of the next inflation readings.
topics.discussionPrompt: When markets get jumpy, who checks the numbers calmly and who treats every red arrow like a personal insult?

topics.title: Apple unveils foldable iPhone
topics.summary: Apple introduced a foldable iPhone design, giving the company a major product refresh while investors watched how the launch might affect its growth story.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would a folding phone make anyone in the studio more productive, or just give them twice as much screen to procrastinate on?

topics.title: Meta launches AI assistant
topics.summary: Meta shares rose after the company rolled out Muse, an AI assistant pitched as able to help users complete online tasks across services.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an AI assistant offers to book travel or sell a car, who trusts it first and who demands to supervise every click?

topics.title: Global test scores slide
topics.summary: New PISA results showed falling math, reading, and science scores in many high-income countries, with family support and digital habits under renewed scrutiny.
topics.discussionPrompt: If school scores drop everywhere at once, does the studio blame phones, homework, parents, or the whole system?

topics.title: BBC faces strike risk
topics.summary: BBC leadership acknowledged a real possibility of strikes as staff push back against pay plans and large job cuts tied to the broadcaster's funding squeeze.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a beloved institution says money is tight, who argues for saving jobs and who asks what the budget actually says?

topics.title: Republicans gather for midterms
topics.summary: Republicans opened a two-day midterm convention in Dallas, aiming to energize voters while Democrats countered with criticism on inflation and foreign policy.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a political convention came to town, who watches for the speeches and who only notices the traffic?

topics.title: Smithsonian chief steps down
topics.summary: NPR reported that Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie G. Bunch III resigned, adding another cultural-institution story to a busy political news week.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a major museum leader resigns, who in the studio wants the backstory and who just asks if the exhibits stay open?

topics.title: Debate grows over AI risk
topics.summary: Researchers, lawmakers, and campaigners renewed arguments over advanced AI safety, balancing warnings about future systems with concerns about present-day harms.
topics.discussionPrompt: How does the studio talk about scary AI predictions without turning the whole conversation into a sci-fi emergency meeting?

topics.title: GPS jamming draws attention
topics.summary: BBC technology coverage highlighted growing concern over GPS interference and the hidden infrastructure that keeps timing, navigation, and networks synchronized.
topics.discussionPrompt: If GPS suddenly got unreliable, who in the studio could navigate by memory and who would immediately be lost?
